A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PFEV research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including Appendices A–K in v1 and A–M in v2.

before.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original optimization experiments, estimator comparisons, and evaluations of parallel, decoupled, and noisy settings.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds LightGBM optimization, DTLZ benchmarks, optimizer comparisons, and truncation diagnostics.

M1.justification: New Section 7 proposes gradient-compatible adaptations, including replacing the hard Pareto-region indicator with a Gaussian-smoothed probability. These are prospective alternatives: the mixture, MAP acquisition, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged, and reported PFEV experiments still use DIRECT.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's GP-generated and analytic benchmark functions, v2 adds LightGBM class-weight optimization on Abalone, Waveform, Pageblocks, and Gesturephase, plus DTLZ1–7. Parallel, decoupled, and noisy scenarios were already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds Random to GP and main benchmark comparisons and qLogNEHVI to the GP comparison in Figure 29. Appendix F replaces the custom grid-based HVKG approximation with BoTorch's one-shot implementation. JES disappears from the matched d=10 FES panels. ParEGO, MOBO-RS, and MESMO remain in appendix comparisons despite their omission from main plots.

E3.justification: The decoupled PFEV population changes from the inherited size 50 to 10, alongside revised HVKG settings with 10 Pareto points and 10 fantasy samples. New LightGBM experiments use an 80:20 split and hypervolume of per-class test accuracies with reference zero. v2 also adds gradient-versus-DIRECT controls for qLogNEHVI and FES dimensions 5–9 alongside the existing d=10 setting.

E4.justification: v2 adds mixture-weight trajectories, analyses stratified by input dimension and length scale, FES dimension sweeps, truncation-volume error versus frontier sample size, and optimizer comparisons (Appendices C, K, L, and M). These substantially broaden mechanism and sensitivity evidence beyond the retained estimator and noise analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 runs, standard deviations for the main benchmark curves, and standard errors for noisy-observation results. The new mixture-weight trajectory uses the existing 10-run mean-and-standard-deviation practice; no new significance testing, confidence intervals, or seed-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds application, DTLZ, qLogNEHVI, dimension-sweep, and diagnostic results. Figure 27 reports PFEV advantages on DTLZ2/5/6/7 but better EHVI and MESMO performance on DTLZ4. Decoupled curves are replaced under revised settings, showing near parity with BoTorch KG at length scale 0.25; this is not a same-setting improvement. Table 1 timings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds an existence argument for the MAP objective's maximizing mixture weight on (0,1], using its limit of negative infinity as the weight approaches zero. Appendix D.1 corrects the beta posterior from Beta(a+m,a+l) to Beta(a+m,b+l). The principal MI lower-bound derivation remains intact.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a general MI lower-bound approach for continuous MOBO, optimized mixing of over- and under-truncation, and particular benefits with three or more objectives. The added application experiments broaden supporting evidence without substantively strengthening or narrowing these principal claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of weaker method differences on high-dimensional, highly multimodal problems, argues that additional MC samples cannot remove frontier-discretization bias, and discusses potentially insufficient variational flexibility. It also explains the choice of DIRECT and explicitly qualifies comparison fairness across GPy and BoTorch. These substantially expand the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix J newly specifies EHVI reference vectors using coordinatewise minima minus 10^-4 and maxima plus 1; v1's silence does not establish a changed setting. Appendices F/M provide BoTorch implementation names and configurations, while Section 6.3 supplies application dataset dimensions and split information. Core PFEV implementation details largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ament et al. (2023), Daulton et al. (2020, 2021), Ke et al. (2017), and Ozaki et al. (2024), supporting the hypervolume baselines and LightGBM application. Positioning relative to PFES, JES, and PF2ES remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits terminology and grammar, changes lower-bound notation from L to LB, retitles Appendix C, and inserts application and gradient-discussion sections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds application, DTLZ, optimizer, mixture-weight, truncation, and stratified-boxplot displays. The original d=10 FES figure becomes three dimension-sweep grids. Main Figures 3 and 5 simplify displayed comparator sets while fuller comparisons appear in appendices; other figures and captions are relocated or revised.

improvement.justification: v1's validation was confined to GP-generated and analytic functions. The LightGBM application, stronger comparator coverage, and direct mixture/truncation diagnostics substantially strengthen empirical relevance and the method's justification. The added existence argument and explicit limitations also improve rigor. BoTorch comparisons remain implementation-confounded, and Figure 29 omits the four benchmark comparisons mentioned in Appendix M, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
